Although the LHC has been instrumental in confirming the Higgs boson and providing evidence for a quark-gluon plasma, the extreme centrality of its collisions restricts its ability to address quarkonium production and the study of hadronization. Furthermore, the Large Hadron Collider cannot replicate the extensive spectrum of primary energies found in cosmic rays, which range from the TeV to PeV scales. Consequently, these facilities are ill-equipped to explore hadronization and quarkonium formation across varying center-of-mass energies. To overcome these limitations, physicists have proposed a new instrument: the Compact Hadron Spectrometer (CHASER). Designed as a fixed-target system utilizing LHC's own 7 TeV beams striking various targets, CHASER aims to deliver the most advanced hadroscopy capabilities at such center-of-mollision energies. This setup will enable comprehensive investigations into hadronization and quarkonium formation using cosmic-like collision energies, thereby facilitating direct comparisons with cosmic ray observations.

This paper introduces an orientation convolutional network (OConv) designed to enhance image classification by automatically learning robust orientation-invariant features. Although standard 2D convolutional networks (ConvNets) are effective at learning spatially invariant representations, they often lack explicit mechanisms to handle directional invariance, which can limit performance on tasks involving rotated objects. To address this, we formulated an OConv layer that doubles the standard 2D convolutional operation by applying filters in both original and rotated orientations within each pixel's neighborhood. Empirical results on the CIFAR-10 and Stanford Cars datasets demonstrate that integrating OConv into ConvNets significantly boosts classification accuracy for cars and other commonly misclassified items, particularly regarding rotated instances.

Point cloud data, which captures the three-dimensional geometry of real-world objects, is widely utilized in fields such as robotics, augmented reality, and computer vision. While Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) have emerged as a leading architecture for processing point clouds by establishing inter-point relationships through graph construction, they often struggle with over-smoothing and over-fitting issues. This study addresses these challenges by introducing a novel, end-to-end learnable GCN model designed specifically for three-dimensional shape processing. The proposed method employs an adaptive mechanism to learn optimal graph connectivity and integrates a regularization technique to mitigate over-smoothing. Experimental results on standard benchmarks for shape classification and segmentation demonstrate that the model achieves state-of-the-art performance.

Recent developments in AI-assisted malware evolution, such as semantic hostless trojans, have posed significant challenges to current antivirus systems. This malware operates without its semantic host, enabling the creation of countless variations through reassembly of disjointed fragments of sentences and paragraphs. To address this threat, this paper introduces a new detection approach utilizing a trigram-based Conditional Random Feature (CRF) model. This method is specifically designed to identify semantic hostless trojans effectively. Empirical results indicate that the proposed model achieves a high F1-score of 0.91, demonstrating strong performance in distinguishing these sophisticated pieces of malware from benign text.

We describe the progress made with the ROSIE Integral Field Unit, integrated within the Multi-Object Double Spectrograph (IMACS) on the Magellan Baette telescope. The system was originally designed to investigate the origins of metals in the early Universe, a goal that necessitated exceptional spectral resolution ($R \sim 20,000$) and the ability to precisely locate metal lines in metal-enriched environments, such as the 4000\AA{} Angstrom Complex. The instrument employs a custom-designed, monolithic, blazed transmission diffraction grating featuring a ruling density of 1200 lines/mm, paired with a standard CCD detector. This configuration delivers $R \sim 20,000$ across the 3500–900 Å range across 16 discrete fields of view, each measuring 0.22 arcseconds. The instrument's design allows for a slit width adjustable from 0.02 to 2.0 arcseconds, enabling observations at resolutions ranging from $R \sim 20,000$ down to $R \sim 2,000$.

This study examines the fusion of two $^{12}$C nuclei at extremely low energies. We begin by outlining the current state of experimental findings and theoretical models, highlighting the significant discrepancies between them. We then detail our recent efforts to enhance the Trojan Horse method for investigating the low-energy $^{12}$C+$^{12}$C relative fusion cross-section by employing more precise spectroscopic data. Furthermore, we present initial outcomes from an experiment conducted at the Tandem Accelerator of the National Research Centre "Kurchatov Institute" (NRC "Kurchatov Institute").

We present high-resolution spectroscopic data for seven planet-host stars, including four with confirmed terrestrial exoplanets, to precisely determine their elemental abundances. Our analysis of the seven stars reveals that their internal chemical compositions are largely homogeneous, with variations in Fe/H, Mg/H, and Si/H constrained to less than 0.1 dex (1σ). This consistency suggests that the formation processes for terrestrial planets are similar across the sample. By comparing our derived stellar abundances with recent models of Earth's bulk composition, we find that the terrestrial exoplanets orbiting these stars likely possess bulk structures comparable to Earth's, with potential deviations in Fe/H and Mg/H limited to 0.1 dex (1σ) and in Si/H limited to 0.2 dex (1σ).

Commercial Wireless Localiza-tion (WLS) utilizing Channel State Information (CSI) has emerged as a promising high-precision indoor positioning technique. Nevertheless, existing CSI-based WLS methods often struggle in real-world scenarios due to antenna pattern fluctuations, multipath effects, and environmental changes, which severely limit localization accuracy. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an attention-enhanced deep learning framework for robust CSI-based positioning. Specifically, the method employs a CSI processing module to extract key features from CSI data, integrates a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2D-CNN) to model spatial relationships within the features, and utilizes an attention mechanism to refine the learned representations for precise user localization. Extensive experiments conducted in actual environments demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms both traditional approaches and previous deep learning-based techniques in terms of accuracy.

This research investigates the unification of unbounded modal logic through the unification of unbounded modal spaces, specifically topological structures, within unbounded modal logic. This approach extends the work done by Hughes and Cresswell in their book "A Unification of Modal Logic" (1972), which focused on unifying unbounded modal logic via unbounded modal relations, or set-theoretic structures. This study demonstrates that the methodology employed by Hughes and Cresswell for relation-based unification can be applied equally to spaces, or set-theoretic structures, when considering unbounded modal logic. This work is the first in a two-part series; the second part will follow.

The concept of edge-tinting on a graph $G=(V,E)$ involves assigning weights of 1 or 2 to its edges such that for every vertex $v \in V$, the sum of weights on edges incident to $v$ does not exceed 3. A graph is termed edge-tintable if such an assignment exists across all its edges. In 2002, Frieze and Mertzios conjectured that every connected cubic bipartite graph satisfies this property. However, this paper presents a concrete counterexample to that hypothesis: a cubic bipartite graph with 1,008 vertices and 1,512 edges that lacks a valid edge-tinting.

This study determines the exact threshold values for specific functions defined on the Hamming graphs, subject to eigenvalue constraints. For any given function, the threshold is the smallest integer $k$ such that every subset of size $2^k$ within the graph necessarily contains a dependent set. The work extends and enhances prior research by Granville and others, utilizing techniques rooted in linear algebra.

COPASI, a widely used cross-platform simulation tool for biochemical pathways, has seen significant growth in its web-based services, which now include HTTP API access for model submission, retrieval, and the execution of basic simulations. In contrast, ShinyCOPASI introduces a distinct approach by offering a web-based user interface tailored for interactive investigation of COPASI models. Leaning on the Shiny framework for dynamic web apps, it seamlessly integrates file uploads, control panels, and results visualization. This interface supports multiple output formats, allowing users to view data either graphically or in tabular form directly in a web browser.

Deep learning (DL) has become a cornerstone in scientific machine intelligence, driving breakthroughs across biology, chemistry, and physics. Yet, the "black box" nature of Deep Learning models introduces significant risks, as predictions made for safety-critical applications in these fields can jeopardize human lives. Consequently, there is an urgent need to develop methods for detecting and mitigating ambiguities in DL systems to ensure reliable, safe outcomes. This study introduces a taxonomy of ambiguity detection and resolution strategies, evaluates various quantification metrics for these issues, and proposes novel metrics to fill identified research gaps. The authors discuss the challenges and opportunities at this convergence of ambiguity detection, mitigation, and quantification, offering a promising research agenda where measuring ambiguity is essential for creating safe and trustworthy intelligence in science.

In the paper, the authors investigate a von Neumann algebra, denoted as $vN(\mathcal{F}(KQ))$, which consists of type I factors associated with compact quantum groups. These factors correspond to quantum double quotients of these groups. The authors establish conditions under which this derived von Neumann algebra falls into types II or III.

Value iteration is widely recognized as a foundational method for resolving issues related to Markov Decision Processes (MDP). However, its application is often restricted to systems with discrete or very limited state spaces, primarily because the classical approach fails to converge on systems with vast or continuous state sets. This limitation has driven the development of level-set-based techniques, which approximate value functions using grids or clusters to address large-scale systems. Despite these advances, achieving both arbitrary grid resolution and fine clustering remains difficult, often resulting in significant memory demands.

This paper introduces a modified Iteration scheme combining Generalized Multiresolution Error Estimation (GMRES) with Iteration (ISI)—referred to as impGMRES—to accelerate convergence on extensive MDPs. ImpGMRES operates by approximating the Bellman operator via sampled interactions rather than exhaustive computation, thereby reducing memory usage. Furthermore, a novel error estimation technique is proposed to quantify iteration-level approximation errors. By integrating this estimator with the impGMRES framework, we achieve memory-efficient handling of large-scale MDPs. Empirical results demonstrate that the impGMRES algorithm surpasses existing methods in terms of convergence speed and memory efficiency.

This paper addresses a problem first raised by Verma concerning the comparison between the symbolic and normal tightness of edge ideals in directed graphs. We provide a characterization of specific subfamilies of directed graphs for which the resulting ideals exhibit a property where all higher powers remain equal; this property holds particularly for all oriented lines and certain cyclic structures.

This study introduces a novel approach to the inverse problem concerning time-series computer simulations, which entail estimating a time-series-specific function based on observed time-series data. The methodology is founded on contour estimation, utilizing data from multiple simulations to jointly estimate both the function and the associated random noise. The proposed solution offers a specific framework for generating these time-series-based contour estimates, which are subsequently applied to create point-wise credible intervals to assess uncertainty. The method's validity is verified through experiments on synthetic data, and it is further demonstrated via application to an emulator designed for solving an inverse problem related to glacier dynamics.

Recent studies have shown that applying region-based denormalization to robust learning yields significant gains in both robust and generalizable performance. However, the underlying mechanisms driving these improvements remain unclear. This paper investigates the conditions that facilitate the effectiveness of regional queries in resilient learning. Our findings indicate that when the data distribution is clustered, regional queries substantially enhance the robustness of the robust loss function. Furthermore, we demonstrate experimentally that employing regional queries with the robust loss leads to superior robust outcomes compared to the standard robust loss approach.

This study examines jet fragmentation within an unpolarized medium using jets tagged by isolated photons to correct for nuclear cold-core effects. The analysis focuses on PbPb collisions at $\sqrt{s_\mathrm{NN}} = 5.02$ TeV, comparing them to pp collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 13$ TeV. The data were collected and analyzed by the CMS experiment at the LHC. Jets were reconstructed using charged-particle tracks and neutral clusters from the electromagnetic and hadronic calorimeters. To study medium-induced modifications to jet fragmentation, the distributions of charged-particle $p_{\mathrm{T}}$ relative to the jet axis were analyzed in various centrality bins. The results show a significant medium effect in the most central events, where charged-particle $p_{\mathrm{T}}$ is less than 2 GeV.

Building on our prior study [1], this paper investigates infinite series involving polylogarithms and colored multiple zeta functions (CMZFs) that do not conform to the standard Ap\'{e}ry sequence format. We establish closed-form evaluations for several such series featuring product terms of Ap\'{e}ry sequences alongside polylogarithms or CMZFs on their right sides. Furthermore, for certain series involving central binomial coefficients squared, Ap\'{e}ry-like sequences of even or even-and-even combined (squares of central binomial coefficients and even terms of the Apery sequence) and polylogarithms or CMZFs, we derive explicit formulas. These results significantly expand the known families of Ap\'{e}ry-related series expressible through combinations of multiple zeta functions, colored multiple zeta functions, and polylogarithms.

This study presents the findings of a follow-up spectroscopic and photometric investigation into the newly identified, isolated, and extremely low-luminosity brown dwarf WISEA J153429.75-104303.3, commonly referred to as "The Mishap." Initial observations by the TESS mission revealed that the object's brightness varied by approximately 1% over a 1.5-hour period, a fluctuation attributed to atmospheric cloud structures. Our subsequent spectroscopy, conducted using the 2.3-meter telescope at CTIO, uncovered evidence of a highly dynamic atmosphere featuring strong vertical mixing, intense weather systems, and a distinct lack of methane, which together suggest the object is more massive than previously estimated. These atmospheric dynamics also help explain the object's unusually high mass by offering a mechanism for the conversion of internal heat into kinetic energy. Furthermore, our data indicate that the object's effective temperature is roughly 1,000 K lower than what standard cooling models predict for an object of its age and inferred mass. This discrepancy between predicted and observed temperatures, combined with the atmospheric signs of vigorous mixing, provides compelling evidence that the object is accreting material from a companion body, likely a second brown dwarf.

This study reports the production yields of pions, kaons, (anti-)protons, and $\phi$ mesons in central Xe-Xe collisions at a nucleon-nucleon center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.44$ TeV. The analysis utilizes data from the ALICE experiment at the LHC, where $\phi$ mesons were identified through decays into Kaon pairs in central collisions with a pseudorapidity range of $|\eta|<3.8$. The measured raw yields for pions, kaons, (anti-)protons, and $\phi$ mesons are $1.06\pm0.02_{\rm{stat}}\pm0.12_{\rm{sys}}$, $0.21\pm0.01_{\rm{stat}}\pm0.02_{\rm{sys}}$, $0.04\pm0.01_{\rm{stat}}\pm0.01_{\rm{sys}}$, and $0.01\pm0.01_{\rm{stat}}\pm0.01_{\rm{sys}}$ per event, respectively. These results are compared against predictions from various models, revealing a significant discrepancy between the measured Xe-Xe $\phi$ meson yield and those of pp and A-A collisions at the same energy.

Interpolating parton distribution function data is essential for parton distribution function evolution and the calculation of hadronic cross sections. We demonstrate that a more effective interpolation method can be achieved by expressing PDFs in terms of generalized sigmoidal functions. Furthermore, we present an algorithm for numerically deriving PDFs that accounts for both experimental uncertainties and PDF evolution errors.

This study examines how sintering temperature impacts the microstructure and mechanical properties of compacted lunar and Martian regolith. Findings indicate that as temperature rises, both Young's modulus and compressive strength increase significantly; specifically, optimal strength gains for Martian regolith occur between 1050 K and 1150 K, while lunar regolith reaches its peak at approximately 1100 K. Furthermore, the porous microstructure of the sintered material consists of a glassy phase and angular mineral fragments, with grain growth observed at elevated temperatures. The mechanical performance is primarily dictated by the thermal effects on microstructure and the properties of the intergranular glassy matrix.

The dynamics of the Rayleigh-Plateau instability for a liquid coating on a fiber are modeled using two-fluid, two-scale lubrication equations. These equations integrate a long-wave equation for the surface, which accounts for the effects of a micro-fibre structure on the substrate, alongside a short-wave equation describing the evolution of the surface's wavy pattern. The system's two distinct spatial scales are the fiber's circumference and the wavelength of the instability on the substrate. The governing long-wave equation mirrors standard models for micro-particle-coating instabilities but introduces modified effective properties for viscosity and surface tension. These alterations depend on the slip length and capillary wettability at the effective boundary between the liquid layer and the underlying micro-fibers. The model's validity is confirmed by demonstrating that its predictions align with those of a bulk long-wave equation for a liquid layer on a flat surface, where the liquid's properties are treated as heterogeneous. Furthermore, to address variations in coating thickness, the approach employs a homogenization technique that yields modified effective values for viscosity and surface tension. The final results indicate that wettability and slip significantly influence the instability's characteristics, specifically the wavelength and growth rate.

This article is the first in a two-part study focused on classifying tensor idempotants within the category of regionally based $\mathscr{sl}_M$ (for $M > N > 2$, and of type $II$) quantum affine groups $R^i_j$. The authors establish a correspondence linking symmetries of these tensor idempotants to a specific subgroup of $S_{M-N+2} \times S_N$. The required properties of the idempotants, which are constructed from transfer matrices, will be addressed in the subsequent paper.

Diffusion models have recently emerged as potent tools for generating high-quality samples across diverse applications, including image creation, audio synthesis, and molecular design. Nevertheless, their application is hindered by lengthy training periods and substantial computational requirements. Although various acceleration techniques have been developed, there remains a lack of a method capable of achieving both universal applicability and innovative efficiency. This study introduces a novel framework for universal accelerated diffusion through hierarchical data representation. Specifically, we leverage the hierarchical feature extraction capabilities of ResNet architectures to create data hierarchies that support multi-grained diffusion processes. Furthermore, to enhance computational efficiency, we propose a novel hierarchical variational lower bound that introduces resampling mechanisms at various hierarchical levels. Empirical evaluations across image, video, and molecular generation tasks demonstrate that our method outperforms current state-of-the-art universal acceleration techniques in both generation quality and speed.

This paper introduces a novel approach for recognizing hand-written formulae, designed to support individuals with dyscalculia, dyslexia, or mobility impairments who struggle with traditional input methods. By integrating pen-based tracking, the system captures the temporal sequence of strokes, leveraging stroke duration to enhance recognition accuracy. The proposed method combines Hidden Markov Models (HMM) with a stroke-level representation to achieve this. The underlying data was collected using a low-cost tablet equipped with an infrared camera, enabling the tracking of a user's pen via infrared reflection. The resulting dataset, which includes over 1,000 samples of complex mathematical formulas, is publicly available at https://github.com/Aniruddha-Sarkar/HMPE.

This paper introduces a novel, non-statistical technique for generating varying speech durations through the median of existing speech frames. We demonstrate that simply selecting a median subsequence effectively creates synthetic speech of different lengths. Furthermore, we show that this method maintains the acoustic characteristics of the original speech. We also examine how this method impacts acoustic modeling and automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems. Results indicate that when combined with standard time-stretching data, using median-derived speech enhances ASR performance.

Spatial occupancy models are increasingly utilized in ecology to estimate species presence/absence and account for detection errors while incorporating spatial covariates. While spatial autocorrelation in occupancy probabilities can enhance precision by smoothing these variables, ignoring spatial dependence in detection error can result in biased occupancy estimates. The `spOccupancy` R package facilitates the construction of spatial models for single and multi-species contexts—as well as spatially explicit models for occupancy and detection—and integrates these approaches into spatially explicit Bayesian frameworks. This package supports various data types, including presence/absence, count, and binary response variables, and allows for the inclusion of both continuous and categorical covariates. Users can incorporate spatial random effects using either Gaussian processes or spatially structured covariates. The package offers flexible modeling options ranging from basic spatial occupancy to complex single- and multi-species detection models, as well as integrated frameworks that combine occupancy with detection processes. Furthermore, it includes specialized models such as spatial roving animal detectors, spatial zero-inflaged models, and spatially explicit latent variable approaches. All examples utilize real-world datasets, and the extensive vignettes provide comprehensive guidance on the package's functionalities.

Skin cancer represents the most prevalent form of cancer globally, with melanoma being a particularly lethal subtype. Early detection is critical for ensuring successful treatment outcomes. While dermatologists currently rely on visual inspections for diagnosis, this method is susceptible to human error and lacks consistency. Consequently, we introduce the Skincare initiative, an interactive deep learning framework designed to distinguish between benign lesions and malignancies by analyzing images of skin patches. This system integrates two primary components: a convolutional neural network (CNN) for image classification and a recommendation engine that suggests similar image examples to support diagnostic decisions. We evaluated the system using the ISIC 2019 dataset, which yielded an AUC-ROC score of 0.929. Furthermore, we assessed its practical utility through a study involving 10 medical professionals, who used Skincare to diagnose cases from the Hammon-10000 dataset. The findings demonstrated that the system significantly improved diagnostic accuracy and offered greater confidence levels compared to standard practice without it.

This study introduces a novel stochastic autoencoder (SAE) designed to forecast future spectra for Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) using future spectral data. The primary motivation is to enhance our understanding of the explosion physics of SNe Ia by enabling rapid, non-intrusive inference of spectral evolution. The SNE Ia datasets, sourced from the Zwicky Transient Explorer (ZTF) and the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope (Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope), were utilized to train the SAE. The SAE's performance was benchmarked against existing forward models, specifically the spectral synthesis code SYNPHOTO and the empirical model SNfactory. The SAE successfully predicted future spectra for SNe Ia with a significantly lower error rate than these traditional methods. Furthermore, the SAE can infer the physical parameters of SNe Ia from observed spectral data with greater speed and efficiency than competing models.

We report the discovery of a dust-enshrouded supergiant within a distant, lensed galaxy at z = 2.09, located 12.9 ± 0.2 kpc from the gravitational source. The gravitational lensing magnifies the star's light by a factor of 1000, allowing us to resolve its neutral hydrogen (HI) emission line with a velocity width of 100 km/s and distinct periodic variations in luminosity and velocity occurring on a 10-day cycle. These observations indicate the star is a massive, dusty supergiant with a mass exceeding 20 solar masses (M > 20 M⊙) and a radius larger than 10 solar radii (R > 10 M⊙). The detected 100 km/s linewidth suggests a circumstellar envelope with an outer radius of approximately 100 solar radii (R ~ 100 M⊙). This finding represents the first detection of a resolved, dusty, super-wind-driven supergiant in the early universe, a discovery that offers valuable insights into the stellar environments and star formation mechanisms of that epoch.

This study examines the dynamics of turbulent plumes generated by a dense, pulsating source and penetrating an ambient lighter fluid containing a high concentration of solid particles. The experimental setup utilized a constant-flux, pulsating plume emitter positioned at the base of a vertical, transparent acrylic tank measuring 1.22 m in height and 0.61 m in width. The lower section of the tank was filled with the lighter fluid, which was agitated by a mechanical stirrer to create a uniform particle suspension. The injected plume fluid, maintained at a higher density, was agitated by a separate internal propeller to ensure mixing. The study tested plumes with flow rates of 0.001, 0.002, and 0.004 m³/s and concentrations of 0, 0.002, 0.004, 0.006, 0.008, and 0.010 kg/L. The particles used were 1.0 mm and 2.0 mm in diameter with specific gravities of 2.55 and 2.60, respectively. The experimental results indicate that the mean downward velocity of the particle-laden plume declines as particle mass loading increases. The observed behavior is consistent with established plume theory, which attributes the reduced velocity to enhanced momentum loss caused by the settling of particles.

The spread of infectious diseases within a population is frequently modeled as a Markov process that, in the limit of large populations, converges to a branching process characterized by the same limiting one-step transition probabilities. For a general measure of infection risk, we determine the critical value of the spectral radius of a specific matrix that dictates whether the disease faces extinction or persists. In the case of homogeneous risk, this critical threshold corresponds to the spectral radius of the hypergraph's adjacency operator, which is modified by the risk's third moment. Furthermore, when risk depends on the size of the largest neighborhood within the underlying hypergraph, the threshold relates to the spectral radius of the pertiau-enrolled (or perturbed) hypergraph Laplacian.

Differential rotation serves as a primary driver of magnetic activity in solar-type stars, yet the specific nature of this differential rotation varies with the stellar rotation rate. As a star rotates more slowly, the extent of differential rotation shifts from the solar pattern (where latitude gradients are steepest near the surface) toward an anti-solar configuration (where internal latitude gradients dominate). This study examines the dynamo consequences of coexisting differential and anti-differential differential rotations. Utilizing local, axisymmetric mean-field models, the authors employ numerical simulations to investigate kination in regimes of both solar and anti-solar rotation. The results indicate that while the mean-field electromotive force (EMF) in rapidly rotating regimes remains largely independent of the specific differential rotation type, slowly rotating scenarios yield distinct behaviors. Specifically, anti-solar rotation produces a stronger EMF that reverses polarity more frequently, generating more intense magnetic cycles with shorter periods. Consequently, the presence of anti-solar differential rotation in slowly rotating stars could account for observed magnetic cycles that exhibit both weaker amplitudes and shorter durations compared to the Sun's cycle.

To address the growing demand for multimodal data in real-world applications, which drives the need for advanced computational methods, this study introduces a novel framework for universal knowledge transfer across various tasks. Originally designed to process pairs of modalities, the proposed K-fan architecture extends seamlessly to handle datasets with an arbitrary number of modalities. By incorporating shared representation learning, the system effectively manages both redundant and missing data while capitalizing on universal knowledge from multiple modalities. Evaluation results on diverse datasets confirm the method's superior performance in classification and clustering, as well as its robustness against the challenges of redundant and incomplete information.

Dynamic partial order reduction (DPOR) represents a highly effective strategy for verifying multi-threaded programs, yet current implementations face limitations regarding scalability and broad applicability. This paper introduces McMini, a DPOR-based model checker designed to address these issues of scalability and flexibility. McMini features a configurable framework that permits users to define custom communication actions, fine-grain interference rules, and communication abstract models, all while leveraging an innovative, efficient dependency analysis. By supporting diverse configurations of interference and communication definitions, the tool achieves extensive flexibility and its compact design facilitates easy extension by researchers. We demonstrate McMini's capabilities through several case studies, including the verification of specific properties on the Java version of the Linux kernel.

The ability to forward messages is a defining characteristic of WhatsApp, yet in 2019, the platform introduced the ability to restrict forwarding from certain messages containing potential misinformation. This paper examines the impact of this policy change on message forwarding patterns and the spread of false information within Germany, utilizing rich, granular metadata from over 1.5 million conversations spanning more than 100,000 users. Findings reveal that while the 2019 updates successfully reduced the frequency of sharing inaccurate content, the overall volume of message forwarding remained virtually unchanged.

We examine a model featuring a general (possibly non-identically distributed) branching population with frequency-dependent allelic fitness. In an average-supercritical system where type A individuals possess a positive initial fitness advantage over type B, we estimate the site frequency spectrum (SFS) under the assumption of neutral mutations. Our results indicate that the normalized site frequency spectrum (nSFS) scales with the effective population size ($N_e$) and the effective branching factor ($\beta_{\text{eff}}$) in a manner that depends on $\beta_{\text{eff}}$. Specifically, as $\beta_{\text{eff}}$ increases, the nSFS shifts toward higher frequency alleles. These findings are grounded in recent advances regarding allele frequency trajectories within branching populations and the coalescent process in reverse time.

Deep learning activation functions are pivotal in shaping neural network behavior, yet their role specifically within spoofing detection—especially regarding gradient flow during backpropagation—remains under-explored. This study evaluates standard and recently introduced activation functions across both genuine and spoofing speech tasks. Results indicate that the Swish function yields the most robust performance for speech detection, closely followed by GELU. Furthermore, a new function named VIGIL is introduced; designed primarily to mitigate over-smoothing issues in gradient propagation, it significantly boosts end-to-end spoofing detection capabilities. Specifically, applying VIGIL to the Anthem system achieved a substantial 10.4% relative increase in Equal Error Rate (EER) compared to using standard ReLU on the AURORA-4 dataset.

We investigate supersymmetric effective field theories (EFTs) of inflation that incorporate the locally $N=1$ supersymmetry and the supergravity framework. By employing an EFT expansion around the AdS minimum of the scalar potential, we identify the most efficient theoretical frameworks capable of supporting slow-roll inflation. These models are characterized by a landscape of scalar potentials, where inflation occurs in their non-AdS valleys. Our analysis reveals that within these supersymmetric EFTs of slow-roll inflation, the scalar spectral index $n_s$ and tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$ are governed by universal functions of the scalar potential's curvature and mixed three-scalar coupling, alongside the tensor mode amplitude. Furthermore, we outline the criteria required to extend these findings beyond the narrow slow-roll regime.

Photon pair correlation measurements are essential for validating quantum optics theories and validating entanglement. This study reports on the unexpected asymmetry found in the second-order correlation functions of entangled photon pairs generated via spontaneous parametric down-conversion. The observed asymmetry results from the intrinsic type-II non-linear non-linear crystal geometry, interacting with the array of detection apertures and the specific polarization states of the generated pairs. Although the effect is most prominent when using a multi-aperture system, it also influences the correlation profile recorded in a standard two-aperture setup.

We utilized scanning near-field optical microscopy (SNOM) to investigate the near-field distributions of planar microwave resonators operating in the sub-THz frequency range. By scanning a metallic tip across the device, we measured the amplitude of signals induced by dynamic near-field fluctuations in the sample. The observed amplitude variations allowed us to map the spatial profiles of the resonant modes, with results showing excellent agreement between the experimental data and theoretical simulations. Furthermore, we detected frequency shifts in these modes resulting from tip-sample interactions, which we analyzed using a perturbation model. This agreement between our model and the measured shifts provides definitive confirmation of the resonant mode profiles. Ultimately, we demonstrate that the developed SNOM technique offers a powerful means for characterizing planar microwave and terahertz resonant structures.
We demonstrate that for every uncountable cardinal $\kappa < \mathbb{R}$, there exists a Borel partition of the real line such that each subset induced by the partition has cardinality $\kappa$.

An agent-based simulation is employed to investigate whether introducing new trading tactics into established, historically accurate market models can generate superior performance. The study introduces a strategy based on fundamental analysis, which demonstrates that while this novel approach yields significant individual profits, it fails to outperform existing current methods. The research concludes that existing high-earning strategies are unlikely to be replicated by agents due to their inherent complexity and specific historical dependencies, suggesting these tactics are not easily arbitraged. Consequently, existing model predictions for historical trading returns remain robust against the introduction of new, implementable investment strategies.

Dynamic protocol identification represents a critical function for entities managing networks, enabling the continuous monitoring of connections to detect and respond to emerging attacks. While the ISO/IEC 8802-11 standard (IEEE 802.11) defines the fundamental requirements for this capability within the Wi-Fi framework, the author argues that relying solely on the initial few dozen packets is insufficient for accurately identifying modern, complex protocols. In response, the IDynamic feature was developed to address these limitations by dynamically adapting the number of required samples based on specific protocol complexity. This paper introduces two novel assaults designed to bypass IDynamic's IDetection mechanisms: the first involves a countermeasure targeting the IDynamic method's complexity measurement, while the second exploits a specific property of the TLS protocol. Experimental results confirm the validity of both attacks, demonstrating that the initial can successfully misidentify target protocols, and the second is capable of falsely recognizing malicious traffic as legitimate.

The effective blocking of magnon scattering toward a proximate superconductor is analyzed. By employing a quantum-corrected Green's function technique, we compute the magnon superconductor-induced transition probability. Our findings demonstrate that quantum corrections substantially boost this blocking effect compared to purely classical magnons. We also examine how magnon frequency, proximity of the superconductor interface, and magnetic ordering influence magnon superconductor-induced transitions.

This study addresses a zero-shot distributed learning challenge in distributed audio classification, where each node trains on a specific subset of data containing only a subset of the total possible novel classes, with some classes excluded from that node. The goal is to develop a centralized zero-shot classifier for these unseen categories using only training data from seen classes, by aggregating locally trained classifiers and merging them into a global model. To tackle this, the authors propose a new method that constructs individual node classifiers using neural networks with compatibility constraints, then merges these local models via a specific aggregation strategy. Experiments on the ESC-50 dataset demonstrate that this approach significantly outperforms existing baselines, which are limited to predicting only in-class unknown labels.

This paper introduces an innovative protocol for generating and verifying $N$-qubit quantum states across any dimension $d$, where $d$ is a prime number. The proposed scheme is both versatile and efficient, utilizing a single comprehensive assay to confirm the fidelity of the entire multi-qubit entangled system against its ideal target state. The assay's efficacy is validated through the successful generation and verification of various high-fidelity maximally entangled GHZ states involving up to 20 qubits on the IBM quantum processor. The study concludes by outlining the method's broad applications, including the enhanced generation and verification of quantum states, as well as rigorous entanglement and quantum correlation assessments for $N$-qubit GHZ states.

Intelligent Reflecting Surfaces (IRS) are emerging as a pivotal technology within ReInV platforms designed to enhance network coverage and boost spectral efficiency. A primary challenge lies in the extensive dimensionality of IRS channel matrices, which is calculated as the product of users' and elements' counts ($K \times M$). This paper introduces a cascaded channel modeling approach for IRS-assisted multi-user systems. Specifically, it formulates channel estimation as an optimization problem aimed at minimizing mean squared error (MSE) under limited pilot resources. By leveraging low-rong approximation (LRA) techniques, the study derives a closed-form solution for pilot allocation. Furthermore, it proposes two alternative methods for estimating unitary matrices using minimal computational resources. Simulation results validate the analytical findings and demonstrate the proposed method's superior estimation performance compared to existing approaches.

This research utilizes data from over 1,000 regional and local online news outlets across the United States to analyze COVID-19 coverage, examining the volume of news stories, audience engagement, and connections with case and death counts. Using a standardized news coding framework, the authors found that regional outlets published significantly fewer stories about the pandemic compared to national counterparts. Audience analysis revealed that viewership peaked in the early stages of the crisis but declined over time, showing an inverse relationship with the volume of published coverage. Furthermore, online readership was observed to rise more sharply when reporting increased, especially during later phases of the outbreak. The study also examined the link between audience size and the intensity of news coverage relative to COVID-19 cases and fatalities; results indicate that regional online readership grew faster than both official cases and deaths, suggesting news consumption expanded disproportionately relative to the actual progression of the disease.

Counting represents a fundamental yet difficult cognitive task for toddlers, typically requiring three years to master. This study examines that progression through an innovative application of deep learning, utilizing a memory-augmented network to simulate human acquisition of addition with carry operations over an extended training period. The researchers observed that the model's performance improves gradually with time, mirroring the slow learning curves seen in human development during childhood.

The paper introduces the "xor filter," a space-efficient and swift probabilistic data structure (PDS) designed for rapid membership checks. The authors provide a theoretical analysis of its time and memory complexities while also evaluating a practical implementation through comparison with standard PDSs like the bloom filter and the compact Cuckoo filter. Experimental results demonstrate that the bloom filter requires 2.3 to 3.5 times more space and the Cuckoo filter demands 1.1 to 1.5 times more space to achieve equivalent failure rates. In terms of performance, the xored filter delivers faster operation speeds, being 1.1 to 1.5 times quicker than bloom filters and 1.2 to 1.4 times faster than Cuckoo filters.

This paper examines the connections within convex geometry involving complex and topological frameworks. The discussion includes the topological characterization of convex bodies through their exposed and extreme points, alongside a focus on the convex structure induced by the extreme point set of such bodies. Additionally, the analytical and topological properties of analytic convex functions are explored, along with a correspondence between these functions and convex bodies. The fundamental role of homotheties in understanding complex convexity is highlighted, alongside the utilization of the Lie group structure of the general linear group, $GL(n, \mathbb{C})$, in addressing problems within convex analysis. Finally, the study extends to convex algebras, investigating both their intrinsic properties and external behaviors.

This paper introduces a novel methodology for analyzing market trends, modeling price evolution as the outcome of microstructure dynamics involving execution costs, share volume, and transaction timing. It offers a theoretical framework to understand trend dynamics and provides empirical evidence using historical data from the London Stock Exchange. Furthermore, it introduces the Trend Index, a new measure for quantifying market trends, and examines the trend index's predictive capabilities for future returns.

While distributed data privacy is a major concern, federated learning (FL) offers a viable solution by keeping data local to clients and sharing only model parameters. However, existing FL frameworks remain vulnerable to poisoning attacks launched by malevolent clients. This paper introduces FLVoogd, a new, robust, and privacy-preserving aggregation method that integrates the Voigt distribution with secure computation. FLLVoogd effectively filters out attacks from bad actors while preserving the confidentiality of transmitted data from all participants. Evaluation results demonstrate that FLVoogd maintains strong resistance against various poisoning attacks, notably outperforming the leading current solution, K-Means, in accuracy. Furthermore, it remains competitive with standard FL protocols regarding transmission overhead and computational costs.

This study addresses real-time Sim2Transfer for navigation, focusing on adapting a pre-trained simulation agent to an unfamiliar real environment without additional learning on location. We introduce a new picture-based adaptation technique that leverages image gradients to align simulation and real-world visual data, facilitating more robust generalization. Testing across three diverse environments demonstrates that this Sim2Transfer approach surpasses previous state-of-the-art methods. The corresponding source code is available on GitHub.

Deepfake technologies employ end-to-end deep learning models to synthesize realistic forgeries by swapping faces or altering speech. While current research predominantly relies on unconstrained datasets for detection, the efficacy of existing detection algorithms often declines significantly when applied to unconstrained media. Conversely, generating artificial unconstrained data for training is both costly and impractical. This paper introduces a novel, unsupervised method for creating synthetic unconstrained patches that remain compatible with existing deepfake detection frameworks. Additionally, the authors present a new dataset, DDFake5K, comprising 5,000 patches drawn from public videos and news clips; these patches are captured at various resolutions, resolutions, and levels of blurriness to support training detection models on real-world unconstrained media. Leveraging this dataset, the authors developed an end-to-end framework for adaptively fine-tuning pre-trained ResNet models to classify synthetic unconstrained patches as either real or fake. Empirical results indicate that this approach outperforms current state-of-the-art methods by a substantial margin, achieving an F1 score of 0.812 and a precision of 0.781 on the training set and 0.801 respectively on the test set.

Recent research indicates that the supermassive black hole at the center of the Milky Way is obscured by a dusty torus, which in turn hides vast regions of star formation. This study focuses on a different phenomenon: the potential for Earth-like life to exist on temperate sub-Neptunes, a possibility that could be revealed through specific transit signatures. We propose that the equilibrium between solubility and gas-phase thermodynamics in planetary atmospheres can generate observable features during planetary transits. Specifically, we examine the effect of varying internal heat fluxes on the solubility equilibrium of H₂O in the atmospheres of sub-Neptunes possessing Earth-like conditions. Our findings reveal that increasing a planet's internal heat flux can create a "solubility gap" in the lower atmosphere, a layer where water vapor is depleted due to being below saturation levels. This effect is most pronounced in planets with Earth-like characteristics. We demonstrate that this solubility gap can be detected via transmission spectroscopy, provided the planet has an atmosphere dominated by hydrogen. The presence of such gaps would indicate the existence of a global high-pressure ocean beneath the atmosphere. Consequently, this methodology offers a novel approach for using transit spectroscopy to identify concealed oceans on temperate sub-Neptune worlds.

This research investigates learning within probabilistic environments using an elastic bionic neuromorphic network. The study examines two specific scenarios: a linear setting with Gaussian noise and a circular setting featuring von Mises noise. In both cases, the input sequence is received as temporal spikes, while the target output is delivered as an instantaneous one-shot spike. The fundamental architecture relies on an encoder-decoder framework where the encoder functions as an echo state network (ESN) and the decoder as a spiking reservoir. A key innovation lies in the decoder, which is trained via variational inference to minimize the mean squared error between one-shot inputs and outputs. The paper evaluates various generative models for sequences, including Hidden Markov Models (HMM), Gaussian Processes (GPs), and a long short-term memory (LSTM) network. The results demonstrate that effective learning of spiking data occurs in both experimental contexts, with notable improvements achieved through the use of a variational decoder compared to standard supervised learning approaches.

This document details the Out-of-Context challenge, an initiative established to assess dialogue systems in the demands of customer service interactions. The report begins by defining the challenge's motivation, scope, and core architecture, then explains the dataset and evaluation protocols used to measure system performance. Additionally, it outlines various interpretation methods for the challenge results and provides analysis from the participating teams. The study concludes by recommending specific improvements for the data and evaluation metrics for potential future iterations of similar challenges.

This study introduces a systematic framework for the verification of A posteriori Generalized Polynomial Chaos (GPCE) expansions solving Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) with random coefficients. The core strategy involves enhancing deterministic PDEs with stochastic dimensionality by applying a univariate weighted Hilbert space to random variables; deterministic residuals are then computed at each GPCE coefficient to ensure accuracy. By linking these residuals to a priori estimation of a stochastic solution's error, the framework determines the minimum polynomial degree required for optimality. An algorithm is devised for constructing an error-controlled GPCE, with degree selection guided by the estimated verification results. Furthermore, an algorithm is proposed for calculating upper bounds on random fields using univariate confidence intervals. Finally, the framework's utility is demonstrated through two examples: verifying known PDEs and assessing a newly developed model for the random fatigue of welded joints.

This study addresses a sequential identification challenge in a partially-observed system where a system's state is only partially accessible, and a change alters a specific unobserved subsystem. The objective is to detect this shift and, subsequently, select an appropriate reconfiguration strategy to restore optimal performance. The proposed method employs a hybrid approach, combining a sequential identification scheme for timing the shift with a multi-armed bandit framework for choosing the best observation-based adjustment. The paper outlines a sequential rule grounded in a data-driven threshold applied to the posterior probability of change occurrence, while an observation selector utilizing a standard bandit policy is also introduced. The effectiveness of this strategy is validated through a numerical example featuring a change-induced degradation in a reconfigurable manufacturing system.

We present findings on the stellar populations of 12 ultra- and low-mass dwarf galaxies, utilizing data from the APOGEE survey. Our analysis reveals that these systems exhibit significant variations in metallicity and abundance patterns, with most lacking a clear trend between [Fe/H] and [Mg/Fe]. While the majority of these dwarfs show magnesium abundances consistent with solar ratios relative to iron, some display mild enhancements or deficiencies. These observations suggest that the formation histories of ultra- and low-mass dwarfs are highly diverse. Furthermore, by examining the [Mg/Fe] versus [Fe/H] relationship, we infer that the majority of these galaxies experienced rapid star formation, with a significant fraction of their gas consumed within 100 million years.

Let $G$ be a profinite group; this text introduces $\mathbb{R}^\infty_G$, defined as the $G$-equivariant version of the classical Eilenberg-MacLane spectrum, alongside the associated homotopy action spectrum $\mathbb{R}^\infty_G$ acting upon a category of $G$-spectra. The work demonstrates that the equivariant stable catgeory serves as a pro-finite $G$-space equivalent to this action, specifically showing that stable cohomology classes with coefficients in an Eilenberg-MacLane spectrum for a topological $G$-space arise as the equivariant version thereof.

Extracting structured information from visual documents, such as invoices and receipts, is vital for numerous business applications. While deep learning models offer a promising solution, they demand extensive labeled datasets that are both labor-intensive and costly to prepare. To address this challenge, we introduce a semi-supervised approach designed to leverage rich contextual cues in images to enhance model performance. By combining labeled and unlabeled data during training, our method achieves superior accuracy compared to solely using labeled datasets. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this technique significantly lowers the monetary costs associated with data labeling.

The interface between EuS and InAs is pivotal for the operation of the EuS spin valve, as electronic states localized at this boundary govern spin-dependent transport. Utilizing density functional theory, this study investigates how varying atomic configurations—specifically, whether indium binds to the EuS vacuum side or indium binds to the EuS side—affect the electronic framework at the EuS/inAs boundary. Findings indicate that regardless of the specific interface structure, in-as-derived states within the EuS bandgap remain sparse. Nevertheless, these gap states shift in energy based on atomic arrangement, and crucially, they intrude into Eu 5f bands on the bulk EuS side when indium attaches to the EuS surface. Consequently, an electronic framework similar to that produced by indium binding on the InAs side emerges only when indium bonds to the EuS side.

This paper presents an efficient method for representing and categorizing all potential pairs of Borel sets classified by Wadge order, along with effective procedures for computing product and projection operations on these relations. Given that the author focuses specifically on classes relative to continuous reductions from subsets of Baire space (\(\mathbf{{}^\omega2}\)), it is worth noting that while continuous reductions are standard in descriptive set theory, this work restricts itself to these categories.

Recent advances in deep learning have yielded state-of-the-art performance across numerous machine learning tasks, yet their substantial memory and energy requirements hinder deployment on devices with limited resources. Although neural network pruning is frequently used to lower these computational demands, existing methods typically fail to maintain the 100% equivalence between the pruned and original networks due to approximations introduced during training or inference, meaning they only achieve near-equivalence. In this paper, we present ClickTrain, an end-to-end deep learning training framework for pruning with fine-grained binary binary pruning. ClickTrain supports various pruning strategies—including channel, weight, and even operator-level pruning—ensuring high performance efficiency while preserving exact structural equivalence throughout training and deployment. By integrating an original fine-grained binary pruning technique with a dynamic computational graph mechanism, ClickTrain enables effective end-to-end training for a wide variety of models. Experimental results demonstrate that networks pruned using ClickTrain achieve superior accuracy compared to alternative approaches while delivering a 2× improvement in top-1 accuracy for ImageNet ConvNets and providing between 2.5× to 9× speedups on CPU/GPU workloads, all with negligible increases in model latency or memory overhead.

We examine modal logics defined by frames with separation, which generalize bipartite logic through a distributive logic structure composed of bipartite sets. By introducing a complete lambek calculus on the distributive side, on the modal functions on complete modal operators, and by relating these to properties of frames with separation and bipartite logic, we provide a complete modal axiomatic system.

The identification of gravitational waves (GWs) generated by neutron star–black hole (NSBH) coalescences remains a significant challenge. Unlike binary neutron star (BNS) or black hole–black hole (BHBH) systems, NSBH mergers produce GW signals that are both weaker and more intricate; the presence of a neutron star alters the waveform through tidal effects, which are marginal in BNS systems but absent in BHBH ones. These tidal deformations provide a diagnostic for the neutron star's properties, yet extracting this information from the complex, low-amplitude waveforms is difficult. This study introduces a deep learning framework designed to identify and classify NSBH signals and estimate the neutron star's tidal Love number ($\Lambda$). The framework employs two components: a convolutional neural network (CNN) for signal identification and a fully connected neural network (FNNS) for parameter inference. Testing on a simulated dataset covering a broad parameter space—including frequency, chirp mass, mass ratio, and $\Lambda$—revealed that the new method outperforms existing CNN architectures in detecting these signals. Furthermore, the proposed method achieves superior accuracy in estimating the tidal Love number compared to traditional techniques such as matched filtering and neural networks trained on matched-filter outputs.

We report the discovery of an ancient hot Jupiter, TOI-5542 b, utilizing data from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS), ground-based photometry, and multi-bandground observations. The planet orbits a metal-deficient G-dwarf (Teff = 5420 K) with a mass of 0.99 ± 0.09 M_Jup, a radius of 1.21 ± 0.04 R_Jup, and an extremely long orbital period of 1,131.6 ± 0.3 days. TOI-542 b is the longest-period transiting planet identified by TESS to date and is the only known transiting gas giant orbiting a star with an age exceeding 5 billion years. Its estimated age of 5.1 (+1.3/-1.2) Gyr and estimated metal-poor host suggest that its formation was driven by core accretion in a metal-deficient protoplanetary disk. Furthermore, the combination of its advanced age and current massive gaseous envelope indicates that gas giant formation and subsequent accretion can occur efficiently even under conditions of low metallicity.

We investigate constrained Markov choice procedures, which involve selecting optimal discrete choices with specific attributes under uncertainty. These choice models integrate external constraints with external or internal uncertainty. For instance, a consumer might seek to minimize environmental impact per unit of utility, while facing fluctuating price variations; internally, a researcher aiming to select the top $k$ items from an unobserved set of $\mathcal{K}$ items, where the full set remains hidden, represents a similar scenario. This work introduces a primal-dual algorithm to address the fundamental dual formulation of these problems, which effectively captures both internal and external uncertainty. The method is supported by a theoretical framework demonstrating its convergence to $\epsilon$-optimal primal solutions, with a corresponding $\epsilon$-level of constraint violation. Applied to scenarios involving price-elastic consumer demand and the problem of sampling from hidden populations, the results are realized through an efficient data structures implementation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets validate these approaches, revealing that the proposed procedures outperform existing methods in terms of constrained efficiency.

This research details a project dedicated to creating an offline handwritten mathematical notation recognition (HMNMR) system. The study reviews the current state of the art in HMNMR and introduces the utilization of deep learning techniques to enhance performance. The proposed approach integrates two deep learning components: a Convolutional Neural Network (L) to serve as a prior for character likelihoods and a Recurrent Neural Network (R) to function as a prior for sequence-to-sequence transitions. The authors also examine the influence of various training strategies on the R network, including one-to-one, many-to-one, and many-to-many mappings. The system's efficacy is evaluated against established benchmarks in HMNMR, and the paper offers a thorough analysis of the experimental results.

We offer a geometric derivation of supersymmetric quantum mechanics (SUSY QM) on K3 surfaces, specifically the expansion of Betti number contributions from worldsheet instantons. In this framework, the superpartners of the momentum map arise naturally as differential forms representing the obstruction to splitting the tangent and cotangent spaces at the fiber level.

Actor-critical reinforcement learning (RL) is a prominent framework for balancing risk-taking and performance, yet its success relies heavily on stable policy gradient estimates, which can be compromised by high variance. While standard practice employs experience batches to mitigate this issue, such limited data often results in poor estimation accuracy. This study introduces a novel Hamiltonian Monte Carlo-based Monte Carlo (HMC-MC) sampling strategy designed to enhance both the stability of these gradient signals and overall learning efficiency. By integrating Hamiltonian dynamics within the trajectory sampling process, the proposed method effectively reduces Monte Carlo variance without requiring additional experience batches. Empirical evaluations across multiple environments demonstrate that the HMC-MC approach yields superior performance compared to conventional baseline RL algorithms.

The Twin Prime Conjecture posits that there are infinitely many pairs of primes with a distance of two between them. We offer a proof by contradiction for this problem. Starting with the assumption that twin primes are finite, we deduce the existence of a least prime $p$ for which the interval $(p, 2p)$ contains no twin primes. By analyzing the properties of this gap, we demonstrate that excluding the possibility for such a first "gap-prime" leads to an inconsistency, thereby confirming the conjecture.

This study introduces a layered navigation framework designed for autonomous vehicles, integrating Immediate Policy Distillation (IPD) with a Sonar-based policy. By employing a blended policy that combines these elements, the approach leverages the benefits of both. While the Sonar policy delivers immediate, data-driven reactions to the vehicle's surroundings, the distillation policy contributes to long-term planning.

Nereid, Neptune's third-largest moon, is hypothesized to possess a surface rich in water ice, yet its specific composition remains poorly understood. This study utilizes NIR reflectance data from the Keck Cosmic Imager (KCI) to constrain Nereid's composition, revealing a spectral slope of -0.0022% per Angstrom and a distinct absorption feature at 1.51 \u03bcm. The presence of this 1.51 \u03bcm band indicates a water ice structure containing a significant number of impurities, likely ammonia, which also accounts for the observed spectral slope. These findings suggest that Nereid's water ice differs substantially from that found in the Pluto-Charon system, where ice is generally considered pure. Furthermore, the spectral characteristics of Nereid's surface bear a strong resemblance to those of the Kuiper Belt Object (KBO) Quaoar, implying that both bodies share similar surface formation histories.

Let $T$ represent the $3 \times 3$ lower triangular matrix containing entries from the field $\mathbb{R}$. This text defines affine and projective surfaces within the projective plane over $T$ by interpreting them as collections of $T$-matrices whose components satisfy particular polynomial equations. The discussion concludes by providing the projective line over $T$ as a foundational case study.

The paper presents an application of Pawlikowski's interpolation technique to produce an eight-characterized second-order structure, denoted as $M$, which arises from an ultrafilter over the countable universe of a countable model of ZFC within the Pawlikowski framework. This structure, $M$, supports the inclusion of two distinct countable models of ZFC, each equipped with an ultrafilter over its respective countable set. Furthermore, within this structure, there exists a bijection connecting the cardinality of these two models. The text concludes by detailing the proof that these properties hold, which relies on the mutual consistency of three conditions: the existence of two characterizations of the models, the existence of the bijection, and the existence of the ultrafilter.

We propose a Bayesian framework for assigning treatment in sequential decision-making contexts with the goal of minimizing regret by leveraging external data. We employ a pessimism-based approach that treats the difference between potential outcome estimates—derived from both internal and external studies—as noisy, drawing confidence intervals to bias treatment toward options with lower predicted performance when uncertainty regarding treatment effects is high. We illustrate the utility of this method using data from the Project ALERT study, which examined the impact of an adolescent alcohol prevention program.

Flat band systems are renowned for their exotic phase transitions driven by strong correlations. When combined with non-trivial band topology, these systems may support topological flat bands featuring emergent topological superconductivity upon doping. However, achieving such superconductivity necessitates overcoming significant hurdles: the lack of kinetic energy retards kinetic superconducting mechanisms, and the flat band's high density of states promotes magnetic ordering instead. We propose a solution to these obstacles through multiple-body superconductivity, a phenomenon where superconducting pairing involves three or more electrons. This mechanism bypasses traditional two-body pairing limitations by utilizing hidden orbital degrees of freedom inherent in topological flat bands to induce effective pairing. Furthermore, multi-particle pairing can generate robust non-Abelian superconducting states capable of supporting non-Abelian anyons, offering a viable pathway for fault-tolerant topological quantum computation.

The Polya theorem on Painless groups of dimension 1 states that if the local compactness of the group $G$ is non-trivial, then the local compactness of the group $G$ is either the circle $\mathbb{T}$ or the real line $\mathbb{R}$. The present paper demonstrates a generalization of this result to the setting of linked groups, proving that for such a setup, the local compactness of the group $G$ is either the circle $\mathbb{T}$ or a group of the form $\mathbb{R}^n \times G'$ where $G'$ is a discrete group.

Presence-absence data, which only take values of zero or positive integers, are common in fields like ecology and public health. This study introduces a specialized distance metric for clustering such data on a continuous scale, derived from the probability of two units sharing a target attribute under a binary independent model. The proposed measure's upper bound relies on the Jaccard index, yet it fundamentally differs by accommodating presence-absence matrices of high dimensions, often encountered in ecological research. Clustering using this new distance was applied to a real-world dataset regarding skin conditions, resulting in findings that were validated through permutation testing. The reliability of these outcomes was further confirmed by comparing them against other standard clustering techniques applied to both the original data and a transformed version converted to natural logarithmic form with one added.

Salient object detection (SOD) focuses on identifying the most significant areas within an image to facilitate efficient visual analysis. Although numerous deep learning-based SOD models have been developed primarily for RGB inputs, these are often constrained by dependencies on RGB-d data, which is frequently difficult to acquire. To address this, we introduce a novel framework capable of detecting salient objects effectively across both RGB and RGB-D modalities. By integrating an end-to-end encoder-decoder architecture with a multi-task learning strategy, we unify the processing of either standard color images or those with depth information. Furthermore, we establish a new benchmark, UnifiedSalient, comprising 10 datasets to evaluate and compare performance on both modalities. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach surpasses existing leading models in RGB SOD tasks and exhibits strong generalization capabilities when applied to both RGB and RGB-D scenarios.

This paper details our team's approach, UM-IU@LING, for the Twitter Abuse Identification shared task (Task 2). Our methodology centers on a two-stage pipeline designed to detect aggressive content in tweets. The initial phase employs a BERT-based classifier to identify individual aggressive entities within each tweet. Subsequently, a Support Vector Machine (SVM) analyzes these extracted entities to classify the tweets as either non-aggressive or aggressive. The effectiveness of this strategy was validated through two distinct experimental variations: one utilizing a comprehensive set of pre-defined aggressive entities and the other leveraging a broader, more inclusive list. Results indicate that this pipeline significantly outperformed baseline models, achieving an F1 score of 68.10\% on the test dataset.
